subproblem.title: Dilation averaging estimate on the boundary annulus of the unit ball
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let F : ℝⁿ → ℝ be measurable with F ≥ 0 and F integrable on B := B̆_1(0) (ℝⁿ = Euclid n), and let 0 < s ≤ 1/2. Put A_s := B ∖ B̆_{1−s}(0). Then ∫_{A_s} (∫_{1/2}^1 F(tx) dt) dx ≤ 2^{n+1} s ∫_B F, with Bochner integrals and an interval integral inside.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n → ℝ) (s : ℝ), Measurable F → (∀ y, 0 ≤ F y) → IntegrableOn F (ball (0 : Euclid n) 1) → 0 < s → s ≤ 1 / 2 → ∫ x in ball (0 : Euclid n) 1 \ ball (0 : Euclid n) (1 - s), (∫ t in (1 / 2 : ℝ)..1, F (t • x)) ≤ 2 ^ (n + 1) * s * ∫ y in ball (0 : Euclid n) 1, F y
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 3(iv) (dilation estimate). It is carried out with lower Lebesgue integrals, which removes all integrability side conditions.

1. (Reduction to lintegrals.) Let I(x) := ∫_{1/2}^1 F(tx) dt.
- If I is not integrable on A_s, the left side is 0 (integral_undef) and the right side is ≥ 0, so we are done.
- Otherwise, I ≥ 0 (intervalIntegral.integral_nonneg) and F ≥ 0 is integrable on B. So ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal converts both sides, and ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff reduces the claim to
∫⁻_{A_s} ofReal(I(x)) dx ≤ ofReal(2^{n+1}s)·∫⁻_B ofReal F.
- For each x, ofReal(I(x)) ≤ ∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} ofReal(F(tx)) dt. This is an equality by ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal if t ↦ F(tx) is integrable on (1/2,1] (after intervalIntegral.integral_of_le); otherwise I(x) = 0.
It therefore suffices to prove
(*) ∫⁻_{A_s} ∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} ofReal F(tx) dt dx ≤ ofReal(2^{n+1}s)·∫⁻_B ofReal F.

2. (Tonelli.) The map (x, t) ↦ ofReal F(t•x) is measurable, so lintegral_lintegral_swap exchanges the order of integration: the left side of (*) equals ∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} ∫⁻_{A_s} ofReal F(tx) dx dt.

3. (Change of variables.) Let T := {(t, y) : t(1 − s) ≤ ‖y‖ < t}, a measurable set (measurableSet_le, measurableSet_lt), and H(t, y) := 1_T(t, y)·ofReal F(y).
- For t > 0 we have x ∈ A_s ⟺ (t, tx) ∈ T, because ‖tx‖ = t‖x‖. So 1_{A_s}(x)·ofReal F(tx) = H(t, tx).
- The image of Lebesgue measure under x ↦ t•x is |t^{−n}|·Lⁿ (Measure.map_addHaar_smul, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).
- By lintegral_indicator, lintegral_map and lintegral_smul_measure: ∫⁻_{A_s} ofReal F(tx) dx = |t^{−n}| ∫⁻ H(t, y) dy ≤ 2ⁿ ∫⁻ H(t, y) dy for t ∈ (1/2, 1].

4. (Tonelli again.) Hence ∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} ∫⁻_{A_s} ofReal F(tx) dx dt ≤ 2ⁿ ∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} ∫⁻ H(t, y) dy dt = 2ⁿ ∫⁻_y ∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} H(t, y) dt dy (lintegral_const_mul', lintegral_lintegral_swap).

5. (Length estimate.) Fix y.
- If ‖y‖ ≥ 1, then for t ∈ (1/2, 1] we cannot have ‖y‖ < t, so the inner integral is 0.
- If ‖y‖ < 1, then (t, y) ∈ T implies t ∈ (‖y‖, ‖y‖/(1 − s)], using 1 − s > 0. So
∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} H(t, y) dt ≤ ofReal F(y)·Leb(Ioc ‖y‖ (‖y‖/(1 − s))) = ofReal F(y)·ofReal(‖y‖s/(1 − s)) ≤ ofReal F(y)·ofReal(2s) (lintegral_indicator_const, Real.volume_Ioc), because ‖y‖ < 1 and 1 − s ≥ 1/2.
In both cases ∫⁻_{(1/2,1]} H(t, y) dt ≤ 1_B(y)·ofReal(2s)·ofReal F(y).

6. Combining steps 2–5: the left side of (*) is ≤ 2ⁿ·ofReal(2s)·∫⁻_B ofReal F = ofReal(2^{n+1}s)·∫⁻_B ofReal F (lintegral_indicator, ENNReal.ofReal_mul). This is (*), and step 1 finishes the proof. ∎

subproblem.title: Extraction of an L²-convergent subsequence from finite L²-nets
subproblem.statement: Let (α, μ) be a measure space (α : Type with a measurable space structure, μ any measure on it) and let f_j : α → ℝ (j ∈ ℕ) be in L²(μ) (MemLp (f j) 2 μ). Suppose that for every η > 0 there is a finite S ⊆ ℕ such that every j has some k ∈ S with ∫ (f_j − f_k)² dμ ≤ η. Then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and W : α → ℝ with W ∈ L²(μ) and ∫ (f_{φ(j)} − W)² dμ → 0 as j → ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (α : Type) [MeasurableSpace α] (μ : Measure α) (f : ℕ → α → ℝ), (∀ j, MemLp (f j) 2 μ) → (∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → ∃ S : Finset ℕ, ∀ j, ∃ k ∈ S, ∫ x, (f j x - f k x) ^ 2 ∂μ ≤ η) → ∃ (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (W : α → ℝ), StrictMono φ ∧ MemLp W 2 μ ∧ Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x, (f (φ j) x - W x) ^ 2 ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 5 (extraction in the complete space L²).

1. Let 𝓛 := Lp ℝ 2 μ, a complete metric space (instance Lp.instCompleteSpace). Let F_j := (MemLp.toLp) f_j ∈ 𝓛.

2. (Norm identity.) For h with MemLp h 2 μ: ‖toLp h‖² = ∫ h² dμ. Indeed:
- ‖toLp h‖ = (eLpNorm h 2 μ).toReal (Lp.norm_toLp);
- eLpNorm h 2 μ = ofReal((∫|h|²)^{1/2}) (MemLp.eLpNorm_eq_integral_rpow_norm);
- so ‖toLp h‖ = (∫ h²)^{1/2} with ∫ h² ≥ 0 (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal, Real.rpow_inv_natCast_pow, Real.rpow_natCast, sq_abs).
Since F_j − F_k = toLp(f_j − f_k) (MemLp.toLp_sub), we get dist(F_j, F_k)² = ∫ (f_j − f_k)² dμ.

3. (Total boundedness.) Let ε > 0 and apply the hypothesis with η := ε²/2. This gives a finite S such that every j has some k ∈ S with dist(F_j, F_k)² ≤ ε²/2 < ε², hence dist(F_j, F_k) < ε (lt_of_pow_lt_pow_left₀). So range F ⊆ ⋃_{k∈S} ball(F_k, ε), a finite union, and range F is totally bounded (Metric.totallyBounded_iff).

4. (Compactness.) closure(range F) is totally bounded (TotallyBounded.closure) and closed in the complete space 𝓛, hence compact (TotallyBounded.isCompact_of_isClosed).

5. (Extraction.) IsCompact.tendsto_subseq, applied to F_j ∈ closure(range F), gives G ∈ 𝓛 and a strictly increasing φ with F_{φ(j)} → G.

6. Let W := ⇑G, a representative of G; then MemLp W 2 μ (Lp.memLp G). The function f_{φ(j)} − W is in L² and its class is F_{φ(j)} − G (MemLp.toLp_sub, Lp.toLp_coeFn). By step 2, ∫ (f_{φ(j)} − W)² dμ = ‖F_{φ(j)} − G‖². Since ‖F_{φ(j)} − G‖ → 0 (tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero), its square tends to 0 (Tendsto.pow). ∎

That scratch file may not persist.

The finite-net hypothesis with η = ε²/2 makes {F_j} totally bounded.
The closure is compact in the complete space Lp, so IsCompact.tendsto_subseq yields F_{φ(j)} → G.
W := ⇑G is in L² and ∫ (f_{φ(j)} − W)² = ‖F_{φ(j)} − G‖² → 0.

subproblem.title: FTC for a Lipschitz function along a line, given a.e. differentiability on the segment
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let u : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n) be L-Lipschitz for some L ≥ 0, let p, v ∈ ℝⁿ and a, b ∈ ℝ. Suppose that for Lebesgue-almost every τ ∈ ℝ with τ ∈ [min(a,b), max(a,b)], u is Fréchet differentiable at p + τv. Then u(p + bv) − u(p + av) = ∫_a^b Du(p + τv)v dτ (oriented interval integral), where Du = fderiv ℝ u.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (u : Euclid n → ℝ) (L : NNReal) (p v : Euclid n) (a b : ℝ), LipschitzWith L u → (∀ᵐ τ : ℝ, τ ∈ Set.uIcc a b → DifferentiableAt ℝ u (p + τ • v)) → u (p + b • v) - u (p + a • v) = ∫ τ in a..b, fderiv ℝ u (p + τ • v) v
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 0 (one-variable FTC for Lipschitz functions, and the chain rule along a line).

1. Put γ(τ) := p + τv and φ := u ∘ γ : ℝ → ℝ. Since γ(x) − γ(y) = (x − y)v, we have ‖γ(x) − γ(y)‖ = |x − y|‖v‖, so γ is ‖v‖-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul). Hence φ is L‖v‖-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.comp).

2. A function that is Lipschitz on uIcc a b is absolutely continuous on uIcc a b (LipschitzOnWith.absolutelyContinuousOnInterval, applied to hφ.lipschitzOnWith). By the fundamental theorem of calculus for absolutely continuous functions (AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval.integral_deriv_eq_sub):
∫_a^b deriv φ(τ) dτ = φ(b) − φ(a) = u(p + bv) − u(p + av).
This lemma lives in Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.AbsolutelyContinuousFun, which GMT.Ch07.Submission does not import, so the proof adds `import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.AbsolutelyContinuousFun`.

3. The curve γ has derivative v at every τ, from ((hasDerivAt_id τ).smul_const v).const_add p. Let τ ∈ uIoc a b ⊆ uIcc a b lie in the a.e. set of the hypothesis. Then u is differentiable at γ(τ), so by the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt) φ has derivative Du(γ(τ))v at τ. Hence deriv φ(τ) = Du(p + τv)v (HasDerivAt.deriv).

subproblem.title: Uniform sup and Lipschitz bounds for mollifications on closedBall(0, 1 − s)
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, u : ℝⁿ → ℝ continuous (ℝⁿ = Euclid n), and ρ : ℝⁿ → ℝ continuous with ρ(z) = 0 whenever ‖z‖ ≥ 1, |ρ(z)| ≤ C and |ρ(z) − ρ(z')| ≤ C‖z − z'‖ for all z, z'. Let 0 < ε ≤ s/2 and v(x) := ∫ u(x − εz)ρ(z) dz; put K := closedBall(0, 1 − s) and B := B̆_1(0). Then (i) |v(x)| ≤ ε^{−n}C∫_B|u| for every x ∈ K, and (ii) |v(x) − v(x')| ≤ ε^{−(n+1)}C‖x − x'‖∫_B|u| for all x, x' ∈ K.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (u ρ : Euclid n → ℝ) (C ε s : ℝ), Continuous u → Continuous ρ → (∀ z : Euclid n, 1 ≤ ‖z‖ → ρ z = 0) → (∀ z, |ρ z| ≤ C) → (∀ z z', |ρ z - ρ z'| ≤ C * ‖z - z'‖) → 0 < ε → ε ≤ s / 2 → (∀ x ∈ closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (1 - s), |∫ z, u (x - ε • z) * ρ z| ≤ (ε ^ n)⁻¹ * C * ∫ y in ball (0 : Euclid n) 1, |u y|) ∧ ∀ x ∈ closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (1 - s), ∀ x' ∈ closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (1 - s), |(∫ z, u (x - ε • z) * ρ z) - ∫ z, u (x' - ε • z) * ρ z| ≤ (ε ^ (n + 1))⁻¹ * C * ‖x - x'‖ * ∫ y in ball (0 : Euclid n) 1, |u y|
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step (2b), stated for a general bounded Lipschitz kernel supported in the unit ball.

1. (Support.) We have s ≥ 2ε > 0. Let x ∈ K and y ∉ B. Then ‖x − y‖ ≥ ‖y‖ − ‖x‖ ≥ 1 − (1 − s) = s ≥ ε, so ‖ε⁻¹(x − y)‖ ≥ 1 and ρ(ε⁻¹(x − y)) = 0 (norm_sub_norm_le, one_le_inv_mul₀).

2. (Integrability.)
- u and |u| are integrable on B: u is continuous on the compact closedBall(0, 1) (ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact, then IntegrableOn.mono_set with ball_subset_closedBall).
- For each x, y ↦ u(y)ρ(ε⁻¹(x − y)) is continuous and dominated by C|u(y)|, hence integrable on B (Integrable.mono').

3. (Change of variables.) We show that for x ∈ K: v(x) = ε^{−n}∫_B u(y)ρ(ε⁻¹(x − y)) dy.
- With f(w) := u(x − w)ρ(ε⁻¹w) we have u(x − εz)ρ(z) = f(εz) (inv_smul_smul₀).
- So ∫ f(εz) dz = |ε^{−n}|∫ f(w) dw (Measure.integral_comp_smul, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).
- ∫ u(x − w)ρ(ε⁻¹w) dw = ∫ u(y)ρ(ε⁻¹(x − y)) dy (integral_sub_left_eq_self).
- By step 1 the last integrand vanishes off B (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).

4. (i) |v(x)| ≤ ε^{−n}∫_B |u(y)||ρ(ε⁻¹(x − y))| dy ≤ ε^{−n}∫_B |u(y)|C dy = ε^{−n}C∫_B|u| (abs_integral_le_integral_abs, integral_mono_of_nonneg, integral_mul_const).

5. (ii) For x, x' ∈ K, step 3 and integral_sub give
v(x) − v(x') = ε^{−n}∫_B u(y)[ρ(ε⁻¹(x − y)) − ρ(ε⁻¹(x' − y))] dy.
Moreover |ρ(ε⁻¹(x − y)) − ρ(ε⁻¹(x' − y))| ≤ C‖ε⁻¹(x − y) − ε⁻¹(x' − y)‖ = Cε⁻¹‖x − x'‖. Hence
|v(x) − v(x')| ≤ ε^{−n}·Cε⁻¹‖x − x'‖∫_B|u| = (ε^{n+1})⁻¹C‖x − x'‖∫_B|u| (pow_succ, mul_inv). ∎

subproblem.title: Finite sup-norm nets for uniformly bounded, uniformly Lipschitz sequences on a compact set
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, K ⊆ ℝⁿ compact (ℝⁿ = Euclid n), (g_j)_{j∈ℕ} functions ℝⁿ → ℝ and C ∈ ℝ with |g_j(x)| ≤ C and |g_j(x) − g_j(y)| ≤ C‖x − y‖ for all j and all x, y ∈ K. Then for every δ > 0 there is a finite set S ⊆ ℕ such that for every j there is k ∈ S with |g_j(x) − g_k(x)| ≤ δ for all x ∈ K.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid n)) (g : ℕ → Euclid n → ℝ) (C : ℝ), IsCompact K → (∀ j, ∀ x ∈ K, |g j x| ≤ C) → (∀ j, ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ K, |g j x - g j y| ≤ C * ‖x - y‖) → ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ S : Finset ℕ, ∀ j, ∃ k ∈ S, ∀ x ∈ K, |g j x - g k x| ≤ δ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 4 (Arzelà–Ascoli on the compact set K_s). It is proved here directly in its finite-net form, which is the total-boundedness half of Arzelà–Ascoli.

1. Let C' := max(C, 0) + 1 > 0, so C ≤ C', and r := δ/(3C') > 0, so C'r = δ/3. By compactness (IsCompact.elim_nhds_subcover with the neighbourhoods ball(x, r)) there is a finite T ⊆ K with K ⊆ ⋃_{y∈T} ball(y, r).

2. Define Φ : ℕ → (T → ℝ) by Φ(j)(y) := g_j(y), and give T → ℝ its sup metric. For y ∈ T ⊆ K, |g_j(y)| ≤ C ≤ C', so range Φ ⊆ closedBall(0, C') (dist_pi_le_iff). This ball is compact in the finite-dimensional space T → ℝ (isCompact_closedBall), so range Φ is totally bounded (IsCompact.totallyBounded, TotallyBounded.subset).

3. By Metric.finite_approx_of_totallyBounded with radius δ/3, there is a finite t ⊆ range Φ with range Φ ⊆ ⋃_{q∈t} ball(q, δ/3). Each q ∈ t equals Φ(k_q) for k_q := Function.invFun Φ q (Function.invFun_eq, since q ∈ range Φ). Let S := {k_q : q ∈ t}, a finite set (Finset.image).

4. Given j, choose q ∈ t with dist(Φ(j), q) < δ/3 and put k := k_q ∈ S. For y ∈ T: |g_j(y) − g_k(y)| ≤ dist(Φ(j), Φ(k)) = dist(Φ(j), q) < δ/3 (dist_le_pi_dist).

5. Given x ∈ K, choose y ∈ T with ‖x − y‖ < r. Then
|g_j(x) − g_k(x)| ≤ |g_j(x) − g_j(y)| + |g_j(y) − g_k(y)| + |g_k(y) − g_k(x)| ≤ C‖x − y‖ + δ/3 + C‖x − y‖ ≤ 2C'r + δ/3 = δ,
using C‖x − y‖ ≤ C'‖x − y‖ ≤ C'r. ∎

Alternatively one can use BoundedContinuousFunction.arzela_ascoli, which requires importing Mathlib.Topology.ContinuousMap.Bounded.ArzelaAscoli. The argument above needs no extra import.

subproblem.title: FTC along rays through the origin for Lipschitz functions, valid for a.e. point
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and u : ℝⁿ → ℝ L-Lipschitz (ℝⁿ = Euclid n). Then for Lebesgue-almost every x ∈ ℝⁿ and every t ∈ ℝ: u(x) − u(tx) = ∫_t^1 Du(σx)x dσ, where Du = fderiv ℝ u.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (u : Euclid n → ℝ) (L : NNReal), LipschitzWith L u → ∀ᵐ x : Euclid n, ∀ t : ℝ, u x - u (t • x) = ∫ σ in t..1, fderiv ℝ u (σ • x) x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 3(i) (FTC along rays; Tonelli with the null x-sections σ⁻¹N_u).

1. Let D := {y : u is differentiable at y}. D is measurable (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt), and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ D) = 0 (LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt, rewritten with ae_iff).

2. Let σ ≠ 0. Then {x : σx ∉ D} = (x ↦ σ•x)⁻¹(Dᶜ) has Lebesgue measure |σ^n|⁻¹·Lⁿ(Dᶜ) = 0 (MeasureTheory.Measure.addHaar_preimage_smul). So ∀ᵐ x, σx ∈ D.

3. The singleton {0} ⊂ ℝ is Lebesgue-null (Measure.ae_ne volume 0), so step 2 gives ∀ᵐ σ ∈ ℝ, ∀ᵐ x ∈ ℝⁿ, σx ∈ D. For σ = 0 the inner statement may fail, which is why only a.e. σ is used.

4. The set {(x, σ) : σ•x ∈ D} is measurable: it is the preimage of D under the continuous map (x, σ) ↦ σ•x. By MeasureTheory.Measure.ae_ae_comm (both measures σ-finite): for a.e. x ∈ ℝⁿ, for a.e. σ ∈ ℝ, σx ∈ D.

5. Fix such x and an arbitrary t ∈ ℝ. Apply Submission.dorag_ha_rb_line_ftc with p = 0, v = x, a = t, b = 1. Its hypothesis holds because 0 + σ•x = σ•x ∈ D for a.e. σ (rewrite with zero_add). It gives u(0 + 1•x) − u(0 + t•x) = ∫_t^1 Du(0 + σx)x dσ, which simplifies (zero_add, one_smul) to u(x) − u(tx) = ∫_t^1 Du(σx)x dσ. Since t was arbitrary, the claim holds for all t. ∎

For σ ≠ 0, {x : σx ∉ D} is null by Haar scaling (addHaar_preimage_smul); σ = 0 is a null exception in ℝ.
Measure.ae_ae_comm on {(x, σ) : σx ∈ D} gives: for a.e. x, for a.e. σ, σx ∈ D.

subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, u : ℝⁿ → ℝ L-Lipschitz (ℝⁿ = Euclid n) and z ∈ ℝⁿ. Then for Lebesgue-almost every p ∈ ℝⁿ: u(p + z) − u(p) = ∫_0^1 Du(p + τz)z dτ, where Du = fderiv ℝ u.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (u : Euclid n → ℝ) (L : NNReal) (z : Euclid n), LipschitzWith L u → ∀ᵐ p : Euclid n, u (p + z) - u p = ∫ τ in (0 : ℝ)..1, fderiv ℝ u (p + τ • z) z
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 1 (FTC along translations; Tonelli for the null set of non-differentiability points).

1. Let D := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : u is differentiable at y}. D is measurable (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt ℝ u). By Rademacher's theorem (LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt), a.e. y ∈ ℝⁿ lies in D.

2. Fix τ ∈ ℝ. The translation p ↦ p + τz preserves Lebesgue measure (measurePreserving_add_right volume (τ • z)), so pulling back the a.e. statement of step 1 gives: for a.e. p, p + τz ∈ D (MeasurePreserving.quasiMeasurePreserving.ae). Hence ∀ τ, ∀ᵐ p, p + τz ∈ D; in particular ∀ᵐ τ, ∀ᵐ p, p + τz ∈ D (Filter.Eventually.of_forall).

3. The set {(p, τ) ∈ ℝⁿ × ℝ : p + τz ∈ D} is measurable: it is the preimage of D under the continuous map (p, τ) ↦ p + τ•z. Lebesgue measures on ℝⁿ and on ℝ are σ-finite, so Fubini's theorem for null sets (MeasureTheory.Measure.ae_ae_comm) turns step 2 into: for a.e. p ∈ ℝⁿ, for a.e. τ ∈ ℝ, p + τz ∈ D.

4. Fix such p. The hypothesis of Submission.dorag_ha_rb_line_ftc holds for (p, v, a, b) = (p, z, 0, 1): for a.e. τ, whether or not τ ∈ uIcc 0 1, u is differentiable at p + τ•z. It yields u(p + 1•z) − u(p + 0•z) = ∫_0^1 Du(p + τz)z dτ. Since 1•z = z and p + 0•z = p (simp), this is the claim. ∎

subproblem.title: Boundary-layer L² estimate for Lipschitz functions on the unit ball
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, u : ℝⁿ → ℝ L-Lipschitz (ℝⁿ = Euclid n) and 0 < s ≤ 1/2. With B := B̆_1(0) and A_s := B ∖ B̆_{1−s}(0): ∫_{A_s} u² ≤ 2^{n+3} s (∫_B u² + ∫_B ‖Du‖²), where Du = fderiv ℝ u.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (u : Euclid n → ℝ) (L : NNReal) (s : ℝ), LipschitzWith L u → 0 < s → s ≤ 1 / 2 → ∫ x in ball (0 : Euclid n) 1 \ ball (0 : Euclid n) (1 - s), u x ^ 2 ≤ 2 ^ (n + 3) * s * ((∫ x in ball (0 : Euclid n) 1, u x ^ 2) + ∫ x in ball (0 : Euclid n) 1, ‖fderiv ℝ u x‖ ^ 2)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 3 (boundary layer), parts (i)–(iii) and (v). Part (iv) is Submission.dorag_ha_rb_dilation_average.

1. (Bounds.)
- ‖Du‖ ≤ L everywhere (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
- For ‖y‖ ≤ 1, |u(y)| ≤ |u(0)| + L =: M₀ (Lipschitz).
- Bounded a.e.-strongly-measurable functions are integrable on measurable subsets of B, which have finite measure. In particular u² and ‖Du‖² (measurable via measurable_fderiv) are integrable on B and on A_s.

2. (Rays.) By Submission.dorag_ha_rb_ray_ftc, for a.e. x and every t ∈ ℝ: u(x) − u(tx) = ∫_t^1 Du(σx)x dσ.

3. (Pointwise estimate.) Fix such an x with ‖x‖ ≤ 1. Put
- g(σ) := ‖Du(σx)‖, which is measurable with 0 ≤ g ≤ L;
- γ := ∫_{1/2}^1 g ≥ 0;
- J(x) := ∫_{1/2}^1 ‖Du(σx)‖² dσ;
- I₁(x) := ∫_{1/2}^1 u(tx)² dt.
(a) For t ∈ [1/2, 1]: |u(x) − u(tx)| = |∫_t^1 Du(σx)x dσ| ≤ ∫_t^1 ‖Du(σx)‖‖x‖ dσ ≤ ∫_t^1 g ≤ γ. This uses intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_integral_norm, ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm, ‖x‖ ≤ 1, g ≥ 0 and intervalIntegral.integral_mono_interval.
(b) Hence u(x)² ≤ 2u(tx)² + 2γ² for every t ∈ [1/2, 1], since (a + b)² ≤ 2a² + 2b².
(c) Cauchy–Schwarz on [1/2, 1], an interval of length 1/2: 0 ≤ ∫_{1/2}^1 (g − 2γ)² = J(x) − 4γ² + 2γ², so 2γ² ≤ J(x). Any weaker bound 2γ² ≤ cJ(x) with c ≤ 4 also suffices below; for example, integrating 2γg ≤ g² + γ² gives (3/2)γ² ≤ J(x).
(d) The map t ↦ u(tx)² is continuous. Integrating (b) over t ∈ [1/2, 1] gives (1/2)u(x)² ≤ 2I₁(x) + (1/2)·2γ². So u(x)² ≤ 4I₁(x) + 2γ² ≤ 4I₁(x) + J(x).

4. (Integrability on A_s.) Write the interval integrals as integrals over Ioc (1/2) 1 (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le).
- I₁ and J are a.e.-strongly measurable on A_s: apply StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right to the jointly measurable functions (x, t) ↦ u(tx)² and (x, t) ↦ ‖Du(tx)‖².
- They are bounded on A_s by M₀²/2 and L²/2 (intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const), since ‖tx‖ ≤ 1 for x ∈ A_s and t ∈ [1/2, 1].
Hence I₁ and J are integrable on A_s.

5. (Integration.) By steps 2 and 3, u(x)² ≤ 4I₁(x) + J(x) for a.e. x ∈ A_s (ae_restrict_iff'). integral_mono_of_nonneg and linearity give
∫_{A_s} u² ≤ 4∫_{A_s} I₁ + ∫_{A_s} J.

6. (Dilation.)
- With F = u² (measurable, ≥ 0, integrable on B), Submission.dorag_ha_rb_dilation_average gives ∫_{A_s} I₁ ≤ 2^{n+1}s∫_B u².
- With F = ‖Du‖² (measurable, ≥ 0, integrable on B), it gives ∫_{A_s} J ≤ 2^{n+1}s∫_B ‖Du‖².

7. Hence ∫_{A_s} u² ≤ 4·2^{n+1}s∫_B u² + 2^{n+1}s∫_B ‖Du‖² ≤ 2^{n+3}s(∫_B u² + ∫_B ‖Du‖²). This uses 2^{n+3} = 4·2^{n+1}, s > 0 and ∫_B ‖Du‖² ≥ 0. ∎

That scratch file may not persist.

For x ∈ A_s and t ∈ [1/2, 1]: u(x)² ≤ 2u(tx)² + 2γ² with γ = ∫_{1/2}^1 ‖Du(σx)‖ dσ, and 2γ² ≤ ∫_{1/2}^1 ‖Du(σx)‖² by Cauchy–Schwarz.

subproblem.title: L² difference-quotient (translation) estimate for Lipschitz functions on balls
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, u : ℝⁿ → ℝ L-Lipschitz (ℝⁿ = Euclid n), w ∈ ℝⁿ and r, R ∈ ℝ with r + ‖w‖ ≤ R. Then ∫_{B_r} (u(x) − u(x − w))² dx ≤ ‖w‖² ∫_{B_R} ‖Du‖², where B_ρ := B̆_ρ(0) is the open ball (empty if ρ ≤ 0) and Du = fderiv ℝ u with operator norm.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (u : Euclid n → ℝ) (L : NNReal) (w : Euclid n) (r R : ℝ), LipschitzWith L u → r + ‖w‖ ≤ R → ∫ x in ball (0 : Euclid n) r, (u x - u (x - w)) ^ 2 ≤ ‖w‖ ^ 2 * ∫ x in ball (0 : Euclid n) R, ‖fderiv ℝ u x‖ ^ 2
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof steps 1 and (2a): the translation estimate inside the mollification estimate (cf. Gilbarg–Trudinger Lemma 7.23, Evans §5.8.2 Thm 3).

1. (Notation.) Let G(y) := ‖Du(y)‖². G is measurable ((measurable_fderiv ℝ u).norm.pow_const 2) and 0 ≤ G ≤ L² (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz). Let G_R := 1_{B_R}·G (Set.indicator).
- G_R is measurable and 0 ≤ G_R ≤ L².
- G_R is integrable on ℝⁿ: it is bounded and supported in B_R, which has finite measure (integrable_indicator_iff, Integrable.of_bound).
- ∫_{B_R} G = ∫_{ℝⁿ} G_R (integral_indicator).

2. (A.e. FTC.) By Submission.dorag_ha_rb_segment_ftc with z = w: for a.e. p, u(p + w) − u(p) = ∫_0^1 Du(p + τw)w dτ. Pull this back along the measure-preserving map x ↦ x − w ((measurePreserving_sub_right volume w).quasiMeasurePreserving.ae) and use (x − w) + w = x. So for a.e. x:
u(x) − u(x − w) = ∫_0^1 Du(x − w + τw)w dτ = ∫_{(0,1]} Du(x − w + τw)w dτ (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le).

3. (Cauchy–Schwarz on (0,1].) Let h be integrable together with h² on the probability space ((0,1], dτ), and put c := ∫h. Then 0 ≤ ∫(h − c)² = ∫h² − 2c² + c² = ∫h² − c², so (∫h)² ≤ ∫h².
Apply this to h(τ) := Du(x − w + τw)w. It is measurable and bounded by L‖w‖, since |Du(y)w| ≤ ‖Du(y)‖‖w‖ (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm). For x as in step 2:
(u(x) − u(x − w))² ≤ ∫_{(0,1]} h² ≤ ∫_{(0,1]} ‖w‖²G(x − w + τw) dτ.

4. (Localization.) Let x ∈ B_r and τ ∈ (0,1]. Then x − w + τw = x − (1 − τ)w has norm ≤ ‖x‖ + |1 − τ|‖w‖ < r + ‖w‖ ≤ R. So G(x − w + τw) = G_R(x − w + τw). Hence for a.e. x ∈ B_r:
(u(x) − u(x − w))² ≤ ‖w‖²Φ(x), where Φ(x) := ∫_{(0,1]} G_R(x − w + τw) dτ.

5. (Integrability and integration.) F(x, τ) := G_R(x − w + τw) is measurable and bounded by L² on the finite measure space B_r × (0,1], hence integrable there (Integrable.of_bound). So Φ is integrable on B_r (Integrable.integral_prod_left). By integral_mono_of_nonneg, using ae_restrict_iff' for the a.e. bound on B_r:
∫_{B_r} (u(x) − u(x − w))² ≤ ‖w‖² ∫_{B_r} Φ.

6. (Fubini and translation invariance.) By integral_integral_swap, ∫_{B_r} Φ = ∫_{(0,1]} ∫_{B_r} G_R(x + (τw − w)) dx dτ. For each τ:
∫_{B_r} G_R(x + (τw − w)) dx ≤ ∫_{ℝⁿ} G_R(x + (τw − w)) dx (setIntegral_le_integral; G_R ≥ 0, and the translate is integrable by Integrable.comp_add_right)
= ∫_{ℝⁿ} G_R (integral_add_right_eq_self).
Hence ∫_{B_r} Φ ≤ ∫_{(0,1]} (∫ G_R) dτ = ∫ G_R = ∫_{B_R} ‖Du‖².

7. Combining steps 5 and 6: ∫_{B_r} (u(x) − u(x − w))² ≤ ‖w‖² ∫_{B_R} ‖Du‖². No separate case is needed when r ≤ 0 or R < 0. ∎

Cauchy–Schwarz on (0,1] (variance trick) gives (u(x) − u(x − w))² ≤ ‖w‖²∫_0^1 ‖Du(x − w + τw)‖² dτ.
For x ∈ B_r the segment lies in B_R, so ‖Du‖² may be replaced by its truncation G_R = 1_{B_R}‖Du‖².

subproblem.title: Interior L² mollification error bounded by ε²∫‖Du‖²
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, u : ℝⁿ → ℝ L-Lipschitz (ℝⁿ = Euclid n), and ρ : ℝⁿ → ℝ continuous with ρ ≥ 0, ρ(z) = 0 whenever ‖z‖ ≥ 1, and ∫ρ = 1. Let 0 < ε ≤ s and v(x) := ∫ u(x − εz)ρ(z) dz. Then ∫_{B̆_{1−s}(0)} (u(x) − v(x))² dx ≤ ε² ∫_{B̆_1(0)} ‖Du‖², where Du = fderiv ℝ u.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (u ρ : Euclid n → ℝ) (L : NNReal) (ε s : ℝ), LipschitzWith L u → Continuous ρ → (∀ z, 0 ≤ ρ z) → (∀ z : Euclid n, 1 ≤ ‖z‖ → ρ z = 0) → ∫ z, ρ z = 1 → 0 < ε → ε ≤ s → ∫ x in ball (0 : Euclid n) (1 - s), (u x - ∫ z, u (x - ε • z) * ρ z) ^ 2 ≤ ε ^ 2 * ∫ x in ball (0 : Euclid n) 1, ‖fderiv ℝ u x‖ ^ 2
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step (2a). The τ-average of that step is already contained in Submission.dorag_ha_rb_translation_l2, and Jensen is applied in z.

1. (Integrability.) ρ vanishes outside the compact set closedBall(0, 1), so it has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro) and is integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). For every continuous g, z ↦ g(z)ρ(z) is continuous with compact support, hence integrable (HasCompactSupport.mul_left).

2. (Representation.) For each x, since ∫ρ = 1: u(x) − v(x) = ∫ (u(x) − u(x − εz))ρ(z) dz (integral_sub, integral_const_mul).

3. (Jensen with weight ρ.) Let g be continuous and c := ∫ gρ. Then
0 ≤ ∫ (g − c)²ρ = ∫ g²ρ − 2c·c + c²∫ρ = ∫ g²ρ − c².
Hence (u(x) − v(x))² ≤ H(x) := ∫ (u(x) − u(x − εz))²ρ(z) dz.

4. (Domination.) |u(x) − u(x − εz)| ≤ Lε‖z‖. So for ‖z‖ < 1 the product P(x, z) := (u(x) − u(x − εz))²ρ(z) is ≤ (Lε)²ρ(z), and for ‖z‖ ≥ 1 it is 0. The continuous function P is therefore dominated by (Lε)²ρ(z), which is integrable on B̆_{1−s}(0) × ℝⁿ (finite measure in x). Hence:
- P is integrable there (Integrable.mono', Integrable.comp_snd);
- H is integrable on B̆_{1−s}(0) (Integrable.integral_prod_left);
- z ↦ ∫_{B̆_{1−s}} P(x, z) dx is integrable (Integrable.integral_prod_right).

5. (Fubini.) By step 3 and integral_mono_of_nonneg:
∫_{B̆_{1−s}} (u − v)² ≤ ∫_{B̆_{1−s}} H = ∫ [∫_{B̆_{1−s}} (u(x) − u(x − εz))² dx]·ρ(z) dz (integral_integral_swap, integral_mul_const).

6. (Translation estimate.)
- If ‖z‖ < 1, then ‖εz‖ = ε‖z‖ ≤ ε ≤ s, so (1 − s) + ‖εz‖ ≤ 1. Submission.dorag_ha_rb_translation_l2 with r = 1 − s, R = 1, w = εz gives ∫_{B̆_{1−s}} (u(x) − u(x − εz))² dx ≤ ‖εz‖²∫_{B̆_1}‖Du‖² ≤ ε²∫_{B̆_1}‖Du‖².
- If ‖z‖ ≥ 1, then ρ(z) = 0.
In both cases [∫_{B̆_{1−s}} (u(x) − u(x − εz))² dx]·ρ(z) ≤ (ε²∫_{B̆_1}‖Du‖²)·ρ(z).

7. Integrating over z (integral_mono) and using ∫ρ = 1 gives ∫_{B̆_{1−s}} (u − v)² ≤ ε²∫_{B̆_1}‖Du‖². ∎

That scratch file may not persist.

subproblem.title: Total boundedness in L²(B̆_1) of Lipschitz sequences with bounded W^{1,2} energy
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, M ∈ ℝ and (u_j)_{j∈ℕ} be Lipschitz functions ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n, each with its own constant) such that ∫_B u_j² ≤ M and ∫_B ‖Du_j‖² ≤ M for every j, where B := B̆_1(0) and Du_j = fderiv ℝ u_j. Then for every η > 0 there is a finite set S ⊆ ℕ such that every j has some k ∈ S with ∫_B (u_j − u_k)² ≤ η.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (M : ℝ) (u : ℕ → Euclid n → ℝ), (∀ j, ∃ L : NNReal, LipschitzWith L (u j)) → (∀ j, ∫ x in ball (0 : Euclid n) 1, u j x ^ 2 ≤ M) → (∀ j, ∫ x in ball (0 : Euclid n) 1, ‖fderiv ℝ (u j) x‖ ^ 2 ≤ M) → ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → ∃ S : Finset ℕ, ∀ j, ∃ k ∈ S, ∫ x in ball (0 : Euclid n) 1, (u j x - u k x) ^ 2 ≤ η
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 4 (total boundedness), written with squared L² quantities. The pointwise inequalities (a − b)² ≤ 2a² + 2b² and (a + b + c)² ≤ 3(a² + b² + c²) replace the L² triangle inequality, and the uniform L¹ bound uses |a| ≤ (1 + a²)/2 instead of Cauchy–Schwarz.

1. (Constants.) M ≥ ∫_B u_0² ≥ 0. Let ω := Lⁿ(B), finite, as a real number ≥ 0. Given η > 0 choose:
- s := min(1/2, η/(3·2^{n+6}(M + 1))). Then 0 < s ≤ 1/2 and 2^{n+6}sM ≤ η/3.
- ε := min(s/2, η/(18(M + 1))). Then 0 < ε ≤ s/2 (so ε ≤ s and ε ≤ 1), ε² ≤ ε, and 6ε²M ≤ η/3.
